cards.headline: Question 5: counting Black's second ko at C18 keeps the tree's S[KO-]; the clean kill through the approach at D19 gives S[A-1KO-]. The checker's A-1KO+ fits neither.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line, marked S[KO-]; the checker said A-1KO+. White 8 takes the ko by capturing Black 5. Black to play.
Black 9 retakes after a threat elsewhere, and White can play elsewhere once (White 10). Black then needs one more move: a captures one stone and takes a second ko first; b is a clean approach.

Counting the second ko. Black 11 captures one stone and takes a new ko first. White's A19 is now suicide, so White can only retake at B18, after a threat elsewhere. Without one, White 12 plays elsewhere, and Black 13 kills. Black needs one threat more than White: S[KO-].

The clean kill. Black 11 is an approach and captures nothing, so White 12 retakes without a threat. Black 13 retakes after a second threat, and now this capture threatens at once. Black needs two threats more than White: S[A-1KO-].

text: White 8 has just taken the ko, and its capture is a real threat: if Black plays elsewhere, White connects at B19 and lives. Black needs exactly one threat more than White, decided in the narrow search area only; in the wider one it stays undecided. After Black's retake, White can play elsewhere once, and Black then has two ways to go on (Diagram 2).

This is question 5. Counting the second ko gives the tree's S[KO-]: Black 11 in Diagram 3 takes a ko that White must answer at once, which saves Black a threat. Describing the clean kill gives S[A-1KO-]: Black 11 in Diagram 4 is an approach, White 12 retakes for free, and on this route Black needs two threats more than White, with the count of one as a note.

The checker's A-1KO+ fits neither answer. It takes Black 11 in Diagram 3 for an approach, though White has no free retake after it. Its held-ko test passed only because barring A19 for the whole search also removes White's follow-up at A19 in the second ko. And its + says Black took first, though White 8 did. No move's grading changes either way, since D18 kills outright at the root.
